title: Quiz 10 — cubic magnon terms and four-magnon damping

questions.question: Where do cubic (three-magnon) terms come from?

options.b: from (S − n_i) v_i·J·S_j^⊥ (and single-ion/Zeeman terms) — non-zero only when v_i·J·e_j ≠ 0, i.e. non-collinear order
options.d: from the Zeeman term in collinear magnets only

questions.explanation: For collinear spins v_i·J·e_j = 0 (isotropic J), so cubic terms vanish.

questions.question: At which order in 1/S does the cubic one-loop bubble contribute to the spectrum?
questions.explanation: (√S)² vertices × 1/(S·energy): the complete 1/S spectrum needs both.

questions.question: What is the tadpole?

options.b: the second-order effect of linear terms from normal-ordering H₃ — the O(1/S) shift of the classical angles

questions.explanation: Σ_tad = −Σ_m 2Re(h_m g_m)/ε_0m; zero in the 120° structure by symmetry, finite in canted states.

questions.question: Hands-on: ed_check() — exact-diagonalisation second-order shift of mode 0 (meV, 3 decimals)?
Hands-on: the tadpole contribution of mode 0 in ed_check() (meV, 3 decimals)?
questions.explanation: +0.077 meV: without it the cubic result would disagree with exact diagonalisation.

questions.question: Hands-on: four-magnon sunset of mode 0 in ed_check() (meV, 4 decimals)?
questions.explanation: −0.00590 meV, equal to exact diagonalisation of H₂ + λ:H₄:.

questions.question: Why is H₄ − H_HF used in the exact-diagonalisation check of the sunset?

options.b: Wick: H₄ − H_HF = :H₄: + const (normal-ordered in magnon operators), whose 2nd-order shift is the sunset

questions.explanation: Its first-order shift vanishes, as the check confirms.

questions.question: Hands-on: triangular AFM, S = 1/2: linear-spin-wave ordered moment ⟨S⟩ on the 30×30 grid (4 decimals)?
questions.explanation: S − 0.2535 (converges to S − 0.261).

questions.question: Hands-on: triangular AFM — 2S·δε/ε of the c_∥ Goldstone branch at |k|a = 0.188 (3 decimals)?
questions.explanation: ≈ −0.118 vs the analytic −0.115 (Chubukov, Sachdev, Senthil).

questions.question: Hands-on: near the ±K Goldstone branches, what do the HF and cubic terms do separately?

options.b: each is ≈ ±37ε (a spurious gap); they cancel — Goldstone modes stay gapless

questions.explanation: The Goldstone theorem holds only for the complete 1/S result.

questions.question: Why is the first-order HF shift [T†H_HF T]_nn used instead of diagonalising H + H_HF?

options.b: strict order-by-order 1/S expansion; diagonalising mixes orders and breaks Goldstone modes in non-collinear magnets

questions.explanation: For collinear magnets (H_HF ∝ H) both are identical.

questions.question: Hands-on: square-lattice AFM in a field — magnons decay at T = 0 …
questions.explanation: Max Γ³ ≈ 0.03 meV (smearing tail) at 0.6 h_s vs ≈ 2 meV at 0.85 h_s (Zhitomirsky, Chernyshev).

questions.question: Hands-on: square FM (J = −2 meV, K = 0.5 meV, S = 1), k = 0.4·2π/a, T = 40 K, grid 12×12, η = σ = 0.2: Γ⁴ (meV, 2 decimals)?
questions.explanation: ≈ 1.30 meV of thermal magnon–magnon damping.

questions.question: Hands-on: the same ferromagnet at T = 0: Γ⁴ (meV)?
questions.explanation: The ferromagnetic quartic vertex conserves magnon number: no decay at T = 0.

questions.question: Thermal factor of the 2→2 scattering channel X + B → C + D?
questions.explanation: General rule Π_cr(1+n)Π_an n − Π_cr n Π_an(1+n); positive on shell.

questions.question: At which order in 1/S is the four-magnon sunset?

options.b: 1/S² — the leading damping of collinear magnets

questions.explanation: Two quartic vertices (∝ S⁰ each) over an energy ∝ S.

questions.question: Which CLI options add the cubic terms and the four-magnon damping?
questions.explanation: Output: *_hf.png and *_selfenergy.dat.

questions.question: Why are Goldstone modes exactly at their zero excluded from the on-shell results?

options.b: ε = 0: the on-shell 1/S expansion is singular there (the correction itself must vanish)

questions.explanation: Results are reported for ε > 10⁻³ of the bandwidth.

questions.question: What does symphase.magcheck provide?

options.b: independent checks: classical-energy expansion of the HP terms and exact diagonalisation of boson clusters

questions.explanation: Use it to verify vertices for your own models.

questions.question: Which part is NOT complete at the quartic level?
questions.explanation: Single-ion quartic terms also carry operator-ordering (S − 1/2) subtleties; they are left out consistently.
